# Document Translator

Document Translator helps staff turn Microsoft Word (DOCX) files from original English into client-ready multilingual translated documents.

## What It Is For

Use Document Translator for forms, notices, flyers, and other Word documents that clients need in another language.

**NOTE:** Document Translator is designed for Microsoft Word DOCX files. PDF translation is not supported.

## Before You Upload

Check that the source English document is final enough to translate.

Small edits after translation may require new translations, so it is best to review the source document first.

## How To Translate A Document

The Upload Document dialog is where you choose the DOCX file.

![Upload Document dialog with DOCX drop area](/help-screenshots/document-translator-upload-dialog.png)

1. Open Document Translator.
2. Select Upload Document.
3. Choose a DOCX file.
4. Open the translate action for that document.

![Translate Document dialog Basic](/help-screenshots/document-translator-dialog.png)

5. Select the languages needed.
6. Start translation.
7. Download the finished files when they are ready.

Finished documents appear in the document table.

![Document Translator page with translated files in the document table](/help-screenshots/document-translator-list.png)

## When To Use Advanced Options

Use advanced options when staff need more control over what gets translated or how English appears with translated text.

If you are not sure, use the basic workflow first.

## What To Do If A Translation Fails

1. Wait a moment and try again.
2. Check whether other languages worked.
3. If only one language keeps failing, **[ask the developer](https://github.com/MattGeiger/williamtemple-feed#contact "underline")** to review the issue.

Some failures are temporary provider problems. Your original document is not lost.
